diagram_math_checks.justification: T_K is the gluing boundary and V the attached solid torus; i:T_K->E_K and j:T_K->V are inclusions. F1 and step 1.2 supply f=(i_*,-j_*):H1(T_K)->H1(E_K) direct-sum H1(V). Step 2.1 identifies the first summand with Z generated by [mu], and V retracts to a circle.

The ordered source basis is ([alpha],[beta]) with alpha=p mu+q lambda, beta=r mu+s lambda and ps-qr=1, exactly step 1.2 and the slope definition. The meridian alpha dies in V. The primitive complementary beta maps to a generator of H1(V), so defining v=-j_*[beta] makes its second coordinate +1 without claiming a new core-orientation convention. The zero exterior longitude image gives the columns (p,0) and (r,1). This is compatible with the supplier boundary intersection mu dot lambda=-1; the diagram asserts no conflicting intersection sign.

All three arrows point left-to-right. Step 1.2 gives an injective H0 map 1 -> (1,-1), so the quotient arrow to H1(M) is onto and has kernel im f. The final arrow is to the zero group. No injectivity of f is asserted; in particular p=0 is covered.

The image columns give p[mu]=0 and r[mu]+v=0; eliminating v gives Z<mu>/<p[mu]>, including p=0 and either sign of p, as in step 3.1. The existing rigorous proof is byte-unchanged and independent of the diagram.
